The proposed answer has the wrong sign. The limit is $-1013\ln 2026 \approx -7712.80$, not $+1013\ln 2026$.

Partial fractions give $f(x) = \dfrac{A}{x-1} + \dfrac{B}{x-2} + \dfrac{C}{x-3}$ with $A = 1013\ln 2026$, $B = -2027\ln 2027$, and $C = 1014\ln 2028$. Expanding at $0$:

- $\dfrac{A}{x-1} = -\dfrac{A}{1-x} = -A\sum_{n\ge 0} x^n$, so this term contributes $-A$ to every coefficient $d_n$.
- $\dfrac{B}{x-2} = -\dfrac{B}{2}\sum_{n\ge 0}\left(\dfrac{x}{2}\right)^n$, contributing $-B/2^{n+1}\to 0$.
- $\dfrac{C}{x-3} = -\dfrac{C}{3}\sum_{n\ge 0}\left(\dfrac{x}{3}\right)^n$, contributing $-C/3^{n+1}\to 0$.

Therefore $d_n = -A + O(2^{-n})$, so $\lim_{n\to\infty} d_n = -1013\ln 2026$.

A check at $n=0$ confirms the sign convention: the partial-fraction sum at $x=0$ gives about $-2569.7$, matching $f(0) = \dfrac{2025\ln 2025}{-6}\approx -2569.5$.

The magnitude $7712.798$ is correct, but the sign is wrong. The proposed residue argument also applies $\frac{1}{(x-k)}$ incorrectly by treating the residue as the coefficient of $x^n$ without accounting for $\frac{1}{x-1} = -\sum x^n$.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 5
